text:
San Jose's new top line is three players who were in college or Sweden not long ago, and on Saturday it took apart the hottest team in the league. Macklin Celebrini, Will Smith and Ivar Stenberg combined for eight points in the 4-2 win that ended Nashville's seven-game winning streak; San Jose Hockey Now's headline was "Kids Are Alright." Stenberg, the second overall pick in June, moved onto that line when Igor Chernyshov went on injured reserve, and Michael Misa has taken Chernyshov's old spot and minutes. Both are among our Sleepers tonight: Stenberg at 60% for a point, Misa at 20% to score.

The Sharks sit fourth in the Pacific, three points ahead of Calgary, which is a genuine change in mood for this franchise. Yaroslav Askarov is a big reason, 5.4 goals saved above expected after a season that finished 19.4 below. The underlying play has not caught up: 45% of the expected goals at five on five, and a penalty kill allowing 1.00 expected goals a game. Kiefer Sherwood left Saturday's game hurt, and San Jose recalled Brett Leason. Alexander Wennberg is day-to-day.

Calgary's season has been harder than it looks, and also unluckier. The Flames' goal difference is -23 on -12.1 expected; they have scored 7.0 fewer goals than their chances usually produce, and Dustin Wolf is 5.7 goals below expected. Losing Kevin Bahl for the season hurt a thin blue line, and the trade speculation about replacing him has followed. The bright spot is Zayne Parekh, who Daily Faceoff wrote "is blossoming into a star" on the power play. Connor Zary is out as well.

These two met on Nov. 2, a 2-1 Calgary win that, by our replays of every shot, the Flames deserved only 34% of the time. Matt Coronato is one goal from 50 for his career. Our numbers have tonight nearly even, 3.15 expected goals for San Jose and 3.06 for Calgary.
headline: The Sharks' kid line meets a Flames team owed some luck
